title-proc.eng: Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP)

description-proc.eng: The Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP) project addresses critical gaps in personal protective equipment (PPE). It responds to the need to keep first responders safe and operationally effective during evolving threats, from CBRN incidents and HAZMAT situations to terrorism, industrial accidents, natural disasters, and other complex emergencies. ACTIVE PCP involves public safety buyers and end-users in defining unmet needs and guiding industry R&D towards solutions. ACTIVE PCP procures R&D services through Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP). // Tenderers are invited to propose innovative PPE solutions for first responders, police, firefighters, and emergency medical services operating in complex CBRN and HAZMAT environments. Following the phased PCP model, the procurement supports R&D up to the development of a limited volume of first products. It comprises 3 competitive Phases, with fewer Tenderers progressing at each stage so that those offering the strongest response to the PCP's technical challenge are selected. // The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement (FA) with call-offs for specific contracts for each of the 3 R&D phases (altogether ‘Contracts’). Greek law governs the Contracts. The GDPR Processing Agreement – if applicable – will be governed by the law of the Member State in which each pilot will take place during Phase 3. The FA will remain binding for the duration of all phases for which Contractors remain in the PCP. There will be no renegotiations. // KEMEA will be the Lead Procurer throughout all the phases of ACTIVE PCP. // Tenderers that are awarded a FA will also be awarded a specific contract for Phase 1 (evaluation of tenders for the FA and Phase 1 are combined). Tenderers are therefore asked not only to submit their detailed offer for Phase 1, but also to state their goals, and to outline their plans (including price conditions) for Phases 2 and 3. // The three Phases are: (i) Phase 1: Solution Design. A FA and a Specific Contract for Phase 1 will be awarded to at least six (6) contractors; (ii) Phase 2: Prototyping. A call-off will be organised for Phase 2, with the aim of awarding at least three (3) Phase 2 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 1 will be eligible for Phase 2. The procurers will validate the Phase 2 prototypes; and (iii) Phase 3: Original development and testing. A second call-off will be organised for Phase 3, with the aim of awarding a minimum of two (2) Phase 3 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 2 will be eligible for Phase 3. The procurers will validate the Phase 3 prototypes. // Offers for the next phase will be requested together with the End of Phase deliverables of the previous phase. I.e., all Contractors of the previous phase have the right to submit offers for the next phase (together with their End of Phase Report). A Contractor must have been awarded a Specific Contract for Phase 1 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 2. Likewise, a Contractor must have been awarded Specific Contracts for Phases 1 and 2 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 3. The maximum total budget for this PCP is 3.650.000 EUR including VAT, taxes and other related fees and costs). // The maximum budget per phase and the maximum budget per Contractor (excluding VAT, including taxes and other related fees and costs) are as follows: For Phase 1 (Solution Design): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €47,043.00; Total subcontracting cost for phase 1: €282,258.05. For Phase 2 (Prototyping): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €483,870.97; Total subcontracting cost for phase 2: €1,451,612.90. For Phase 3 (Original development and testing): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €604,838.71; Total subcontracting cost for phase 3: €1,209,677.42. For Phase 1, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of Tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 2, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best Tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // Unless otherwise stated in the Call Off for Phase 3, contracts for Phase 3 will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. The exact number of contracts finally awarded will thus depend on the prices offered and the number of tenders passing the evaluation. The lower the offered price of Tenders, the more contracts can be awarded. However, the total value of the contracts awarded can also be lower than initially expected if there are fewer tenders than expected that meet the minimum evaluation criteria. // As leftover budget from the previous phase can be transferred to the next phase(s), the total budget available for Phases 2 and/or 3 may eventually be higher than stated here (but the maximum budget per Contractor for Phases 2 and 3 will remain the same). // Further information on ACTIVE PCP as well as the Tender Documents can be found at https://www.activepcp.eu/

title-proc.eng: Interpretation Services

description-proc.eng: The Contracting Authority Harstad municipality shall, on behalf of Harstad, Kvæfjord, Tjeldsund, Lødingen and Narvik municipalities, hold this competition. Harstad municipality is responsible for the implementation of the competition. This tender contest includes all 5 municipalities. The municipalities are independent legal entities and will enter into separate contracts. Background The existing agreement on interpretation services expires 10 November 2026 and a new framework agreement shall be established. The need for interpretation services is stable and is expected to persist, at the same time that the requirements for documented competence and proper handling of confidential information mean that we must have clear contractual frameworks, processes for ordering and mechanisms for quality assurance. We assume that in the current situation we have varying types of assignments (planned meetings, acute events, short telephone assignments and more demanding calls). This makes it necessary with a contract structure that both supports high availability and gives us control over the competence used in each assignment. The contracting authority needs to ensure continued access to interpretation services that support reliable and effective communication in the face of users, patients, inhabitants or other persons with a need for language assistance. The services are important for safeguarding correct information exchange, equal service provision and good case handling. The new framework agreement shall give the contracting authority predictable access to necessary interpretation services within different interpretation forms and facilitate flexible orders suitable for varying needs. The need includes interpretation via telephone and monitor (video interpretation), as well as on-site interpretation at physical meetings. In addition there is a need for written translations (translator/translation) if needed. Description of the assignment The procurement is for a framework agreement for the provision of interpretation services. The delivery shall include: The procurement is for the establishment of parallel framework agreements with three tenderers for the following services: Interpretation by telephone or via monitor/video Attendance in the municipality ́s premises or another agreed location. Translator services (written translations) The contracting authority would like to establish parallel framework agreements with several tenderers. Tenderers will be ranked according to the score achieved in accordance with the award criteria. The tenderer who achieves the highest score (called supplier 1) shall, as a main rule, be contacted first and will be awarded call-offs if this tenderer has the requested interpreter available. If tenderer 1 does not have available capacity or cannot offer the requested interpreter, the tenderer who has achieved the second highest score is contacted (supplier 2), and so on depending on how many suppliers the contracting authority thinks it is appropriate to offer a contract. The ranking of the tenderers will be based on the stated award criteria. The aim of the framework agreement is to cover the contracting authority ́s ongoing need for qualified language assistance across different situations and disciplines. A system is requested that can handle orders within the relevant interpreter forms and contribute to the contracting authority getting access to relevant services when the needs arise. The estimated contract value is NOK 14,500,000 for all municipalities in the contract period. This is an estimate based on the available information on consumption in the period 2022-2026 and is not binding for the municipalities. Estimate distributed per municipality: Harstad NOK 5,600,000 - maximum 6,300,000 Sounding NOK 600,000 - maximum 1,000,000. Kvæfjord NOK 1,300,000 - maximum 1,600,000. Tjeldsund NOK 1,500,000 - maximum 2,000,000. Narvik NOK 5,600,000 - maximum 6,300,000 Most of the assignments are within telephone interpretation/monitor interpreters. This type of assignment amounted to approximately 85% of the contract sum. The majority of assignments for Harstad municipality will be for doctors' offices, the unit for integration, the child welfare service, the home care service and the school and nurseries. Using interpreters, the choice between the different categories will be affected by many variables, including which entity orders, the assignment ́s length and complexity, any requests that the external parties in the case may have the type of interpreter that is used etc. There are also slightly different practices in the municipalities as regards how much of the total number of assignments are used on remote interpreters (telephone interpretation/monitor interpreter), on-site interpretation and translations. The distribution within the different services can therefore change in the contract period, depending on future needs. The framework agreement has an estimated maximum value of up to NOK 17,200,000 excluding VAT. The stated value is an estimate and does not involve any obligations to buy beyond the actual need in the contract period.

description-proc.eng: Leading Healthcare Providers (LHP) Skillnet is seeking to partner with one or more Higher Education Institutions to deliver a Level 9 Postgraduate Certificate in Nursing Home Management specifically designed for leaders working within Ireland's nursing home sector. This initiative, fully funded by the Department of Health, aims to strengthen leadership, governance and management capability across nursing homes through the provision of accredited postgraduate education tailored to the Irish residential care sector. The initiative will provide one fully funded place for every nursing home in Ireland over the lifetime of the programme. The initial phase of the initiative will commence in 2026, this procurement relates to the continued national rollout of the initiative during 2027 and 2028. Skillnet Ireland is funded through the National Training Fund by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science. Of the 70+ Skillnet Ireland Learning Networks, LHP Skillnet is the only Network dedicated exclusively to supporting the private healthcare sector. We do this through the provision of high-quality, sector-led, subsidised training, education, research and workforce development. Skillnet Ireland, on behalf of LHP Skillnet, has been awarded this contract by the Department of Health to manage the rollout of the Nursing Home Leadership Education and Development (NH-LEAD) Initiative. The aim of the initiative is to strengthen the leadership capability of nursing home managers and senior leaders, supporting excellence in governance, regulatory compliance, quality improvement and person-centred care. Through collaboration with one or more Higher Education Institutions, the initiative will equip leaders with the knowledge, skills and professional competencies required to respond to the increasingly complex operational, regulatory and strategic demands of residential care services.

title-proc.eng: Intention notice - planned contract amendment for Sakshaug school

description-proc.eng: Contract: Development and renovation of Sakshaug school Supplier: FuglesangDahl AS 1. Purpose of the notice Inderøy municipality hereby announces its intention to enter into an agreement for a change of existing contract with FuglesangDahl AS regarding the development and renovation of Sakshaug school. The original contract was signed 17 February 2026 after a competition announced 4 December 2025. The original contract value, including options, amounts to NOK 96,715,520 excluding VAT. The notice will be published in order to ensure transparency around the planned contract amendment and in accordance with the recommendation in the legal assessment that the municipality has obtained. 2. Background for the change in contract The contract is for the development and renovation of Sakshaug school. After the demolition and renovation work has started, extensive humidity and rot damage has been uncovered, as well as a significantly poorer technical condition in parts of the existing buildings than was assumed by the execution of the competition. The conditions are largely uncovered in hidden constructions after the work was started. Based on the uncovered conditions, the municipality has assessed that further renovation of the building part in question is not the most appropriate or justifiable system. The municipality has therefore decided to replace the planned renovation with demolition and construction of a new extension that safeguards the same functional needs that were the basis for the original procurement. The change applies to the same project, location and same purpose as the original contract. 3. Description of the contract amendment. The planned change means that the work connected to the renovation of the relevant part of the school building expires and is replaced with a demolition and the construction of a new building integrated in the ongoing school project. The value of the contract amendment is calculated to: NOK 39,003,000 excluding VAT. This amounts to approx. 40.3% of the original contract value, including options for NOK 96,715,520 excluding VAT, and is thus within the limit of 50% according to the public procurement regulations § 28-1. 4. Legal basis Inderøy municipality considers that the contract amendment can be implemented pursuant to the Public Procurement Regulations (FOA) § 28-1 first section, letters c and d. The municipality has obtained a legal assessment from Tor Kristian Lånke of Arntzen Grette. Note dated 10 September 2026 concluded that there are good reasons to consider the new building a necessary additional delivery, and that the need for the change is due to conditions as a act that the contracting authority could not predict at the time of the competition. Furthermore, consideration is being made that the procurement ́s overall character is not changed and that the terms for a contract amendment without a new competition are therefore likely met. The municipality particularly places emphasis on the following conditions: • Comprehensive humidity, rot and construction damage has been uncovered, which was first known after the work started. • The municipality carried out reviews and condition assessments before the competition, with assistance from external consultants. The conditions that have now been uncovered were largely in hidden constructions. • The new building will take care of the same function and need that the renovation part was originally supposed to cover. • The work is included in an ongoing project with considerable technical and functional dependencies between new and existing building parts, including ventilation, HVAC, electro, automation and control systems. • A supplier change will lead to considerable technical challenges, complicated interface, delays and considerable additional costs. • The overall character of the procurement is not changed, as the project ́s purpose, function and location are the same as in the original contract. • Considerable costs when terminating and publishing a new competition: The municipality considers it is not practically possible to publish a tender contest for only the relevant building part. The real alternative would therefore be to terminate the existing contract and execute a new combined competition. The termination costs are estimated to approx. NOK 17 million, in addition to costs connected to new competition implementation, engineering design, delays and risk of increased contract costs. The project has already come a long way in its implementation, with, among other things, the completed ring wall and ordered construction elements, which further reinforces the economic consequences of a termination. At the same time, with this, it is challenging to create a new competition where contractors have similar information access. The municipality has also assessed that delays in the project can result in considerable ongoing additional costs connected to the contractor's organisation and progress. In total we are talking about costs of about 30 million. Based on this, the municipality ́s assessment is that the contract amendment can be implemented without a new competition in accordance with PPR § 28-1 first section, letter c and d.

title-proc.eng: Traceability of Chemicals in Plastics and in Plastic Products

description-proc.eng: The Nordic program to reduce plastic pollution 2025-2027 under the Nordic Council of Ministers for the Environment and Climate is administered by the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment. The program is launching a call for tenders for a project on the traceability of chemicals in plastics and plastic products. Chemicals of concern in plastics pose significant challenges for health, the environment and the safe functioning of circular value chains. Effective traceability enables regulators and industry to identify and control chemicals of concern, improve the safety and transparency of recycled plastics, strengthen monitoring, reporting and compliance, support accurate classification and control of plastic-related trade and reduce data gaps and inconsistencies across value chains. There is a need for a consolidated global overview of the methods, approaches, and systems currently used to promote traceability of chemicals in plastics and plastic products along value chains. This project aims to identify practical, implementable and globally relevant options for improving the traceability of chemicals in plastics and in plastic products, providing targeted input to the ongoing Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) and supporting future plastic treaty implementation. It is also relevant for targets under the Global Framework on Chemicals, GFC, as well as the Stockholm Convention. The project will consolidate and assess existing regulatory, technical and sectoral approaches across major jurisdictions including the EU, USA, China, Brazil, South Africa and selected Middle Eastern countries, and as far as possible seek to translate these into prioritised recommendations for increased transparency. The outcome will be communicated as a publicly available report. Project output should be issued through NordPub according to the guidelines of the Nordic Council of Ministers. title-proc.eng: Voluntary Ex Ante Transparency Notice for the Procurement of a MIRO Laser Analyzer

description-proc.eng: NMBU intends to enter into a contract for the procurement of a MIRO MGA analyzer with Bruker Nordic AB. The gas analyzer will be used in an international research collaboration aimed at comparing nitrogen turnover and nitrogen losses across experimental sites in several countries. A fundamental requirement of the project is that the data collected at the different sites must be directly comparable. As part of the project's methodology, a common measurement platform has been established at the reference site SmartField in Denmark. This site uses a MIRO MGA analyzer, and the project's measurement protocols, calibration procedures, data-processing workflows, and quality assurance systems have been developed around this platform. To ensure scientific comparability between sites, the analyzer must be compatible with the existing reference platform in terms of: optical measurement technology; spectral processing and data analysis; software and data-processing workflows; calibration protocols; and operation, maintenance, and technical support. The use of an alternative instrument platform would mean that measurement data could not be directly compared with data from the reference site without introducing significant methodological uncertainty. This could compromise the achievement of the project's research objectives and reduce the value of the data collected. The proposed instrument (MIRO MGA10-GP C2 NO III) enables the simultaneous measurement of N₂O, NH₃, NO, NO₂, CH₄, CO₂, O₃, OCS, and H₂O on a single platform and within the same measurement system. This is the configuration on which the AgNUE collaboration is based. In light of the project's requirements for standardization and compatibility with the existing reference equipment, NMBU considers that only one supplier can meet the functional requirements. NMBU therefore considers that the conditions set out in Section 13-4(b)(2) of the Norwegian Public Procurement Regulations (FOA) are fulfilled. Any objections to the intended contract award must be submitted to the contracting authority by email to innkjop@nmbu.no no later than 28 October 2026.

description-proc.eng: The Contract comprises the operation and maintenance of the complete system of the Copenhagen Metro, metro lines M1, M2, M3 and M4 (the “O&M contract”). Additionally, as further described in the tender material, spare parts to certain systems will be available via a contract which Metroselskabet has entered into separately. The O&M Provider is expected to be entrusted with the full responsibility for the daily operation and the majority of the maintenance of assets forming part of the metro system, including provision of spare parts and consumables. The O&M Provider’s services, tasks, etc. under the O&M contract are, on an overall level, expected to include, but not be limited to: - Traffic operations, including operation of traffic systems and staffing. - Passenger services, e.g. traffic information and customer service. - Maintenance of assets, including preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, provision of spare parts, obsolescence management, cleaning, maintenance optimisation, etc.- Information technology services, including cyber security. - Ticketing and passenger counting. - Communication based on communication plans and strategies. - Organisation and management services, e.g. human ressource management, management of additional services, management of third-party works, technology management, data management, quality management, configuration management, railway safety management, operational railway access management, security and resilience management, occupational health and safety management (OHS), environmental management energy and carbon management and risk management. - Reporting, planning, documentation, etc., including e.g. delivery of variousreports at certain intervals, provision of other information, and compilation, updating and maintenance of documentation. - Services in the mobilisation phase and in connection with the expiry of the O&M contract (demobilization), including certain transitional services to assist in the mobilisation of a potential new O&M Provider. In addition, the O&M Provider may be requested to perform additional tasks and projects in relation to the metro system, e.g. development / improvement of assets, on an optional basis. Furthermore, the O&M Provider may be requested to participate in and provide services / deliverables in relation to a number of larger investment / reinvestment projects and other third-party projects in relation to the metro system during the O&M contract period that are expected to be subject to separate procurements / contracts. These projects are expected to include replacement of rolling stock and signaling for the M1 and M2. The Danish Transfer of Undertakings Act (Act no. 710 of 20 August 2002 on the rights of employees in connection with transfer of undertaking as amended) applies to this contract. This entails that employees of the current O&M provider and subcontractors will transfer to the O&M Provider on the same terms as the employees were employed by the current O&M provider and subcontractors pursuant to the provisions in the Danish Transfer of Undertakings Act subsequent to the O&M Provider’s commencement ofoperation and maintenance of the Copenhagen Metro M1-M4. The duration of the O&M contract is expected to be 12 years (excluding the mobilisation period) with options for extension for a total of 3 years. After the expiry of the operation periode, the O&M Provider must, to a limited extent, provide assistance to Metroselskabet and/or to a potential new O&M provider in relation to the operation and maintenance of the Metro.

Indonesia generates approximately 70 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually, of which an estimated 50-60% is mismanaged. Only 10-15% of plastic waste is recycled; the remainder is disposed of in uncontrolled landfills or leaks into the environment. Packaging waste is the most challenging stream. To date, no comprehensive legal framework for EPR has been established, but mandatory EPR for packaging is widely recognised by the GoI and the private sector as one central policy instrument to internalise the costs of packaging waste, mobilise private capital for collection and recycling infrastructure, and establish a level playing field across obligated producers. Indonesia has built a credible legal foundation on which EPR can be implemented. A new Presidential Decree on Waste Management (JAKSTRANAS) as well as a revised MoE Ministerial Regulation on the implementation of EPR are expected for late 2026. These would outline mandatory EPR for packaging and its modalities, marking a milestone in reforming waste management. These regulations will also form the foundation for this assignment to assist the establishment of a mandatory producer registry. A mandatory registry is important for establishing a level playing field among producers, calibrate the system based on good data, allow appropriate fee setting, estimate the infrastructure requirements and allow effective monitoring and enforcement of the regulations. The objective of this assignment is to develop a concept and strategy for the establishment of a professional, modern EPR Registry for Packaging, in line with international best practice and adjusted to the local context and latest regulatory developments in Indonesia, and to facilitate its implementation through guidance and capacity development. With this, it will contribute to supporting the Government of Indonesia in addressing packaging waste pollution through EPR. The assignment comprises the following work packages: Work package 1: EPR Registry Concept & Strategy Development This work package is the cornerstone of the contract. It encompasses a baseline analysis, the development of the concept and strategy for the EPR Registry in Indonesia. Work package 2: Capacity Development & Private Sector Consultations This work package comprises specific capacity development measures like trainings and workshops with public institutions on the development and implementation of the EPR registry concept as well as stakeholder consultations with the private sector in order to make the implementation of the system viable. Work package 3: (On Demand) Advisory Services for the Implementation of EPR This work package comprises more general, demand-based capacity development of the implementation of EPR in general.
